daily_reality.summary: Marine engineers design internal ship systems (propulsion, electrical, steering). Naval architects design hull form, structure, and stability. They work in offices, manufacturing floors, and at sea, designing everything from cargo ships to military vessels and recreational boats.
typical_tasks: Design ship hull forms, structures, and stability systems (naval architects)
Design propulsion, electrical, and mechanical systems (marine engineers)
Conduct hydrodynamic analysis and computational fluid dynamics (CFD)
Perform structural analysis using finite element methods (FEA)
Develop ship specifications and contract documentation
Ensure compliance with classification society rules and regulations
Conduct damage stability and intact stability assessments
Design marine renewable energy systems (offshore wind, wave energy)
Prepare weight estimates and trim/stability calculations
daily_reality.seasonality: Long project cycles (years for major vessels). Government contracting follows fiscal year. Yacht/recreational boat design may have seasonal patterns.

regulatory.summary: Regulated by USCG, classification societies (ABS, DNV, Lloyd's), and international maritime conventions (IMO SOLAS, MARPOL). PE licensure available in naval architecture/marine engineering.

key_laws.name: MARPOL
key_laws.description: International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships

key_laws.name: USCG Regulations (46 CFR)
key_laws.description: US Coast Guard vessel safety and inspection standards

key_laws.name: Classification Society Rules (ABS, DNV, Lloyd's)
key_laws.description: Vessel design, construction, and maintenance standards

requirements: Bachelor's degree in Naval Architecture, Marine Engineering, or Ocean Engineering
PE licensure optional (FE + PE Naval Architecture/Marine Engineering exam)
USCG license for seagoing marine engineers
certifications: PE in Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering
USCG Marine Engineer License (for seagoing engineers)

regulatory.penalties: Non-compliance with classification rules prevents vessel operation. USCG deficiencies can result in vessel detention. IMO flag state enforcement.

tools.summary: Specialized naval architecture and marine engineering CAD, CFD, FEA, and stability software for vessel design and analysis.

primary_tools.name: NAPA / Maxsurf
primary_tools.description: Naval architecture design suite — stability, resistance, structural analysis

primary_tools.name: ANSYS / ABAQUS
primary_tools.description: Finite element analysis for structural design

secondary_tools: Microsoft Excel for weight tracking and stability
Aveva Marine / Cadmatic for 3D ship design
pain_points: Long design cycles requiring patience and attention to detail
Integration between different software tools in the design chain
Limited number of specialized naval architecture software vendors
Translating complex regulations into design requirements

terminology.summary: Maritime and naval architecture terminology with specific focus on vessel design, stability, and classification.

terms.displacement: Weight of water displaced by vessel (equals vessel weight)
terms.intact stability: Stability with no damage to hull
terms.damage stability: Stability after flooding from hull breach
terms.hull girder: Ship structure treated as a beam
terms.resistance: Force opposing vessel motion through water
terms.classification: Process of verifying vessel meets safety standards
terms.SNAME: Society of Naval Architects and Marine Engineers

career_psychology.summary: Niche engineering specialty with median salary $106K and 6% projected growth. Combines engineering with maritime industry passion. Long project cycles provide deep engagement. Limited number of programs and employers.
career_path: Bachelor's in Naval Architecture / Marine Engineering / Ocean Engineering
fears: Design error leading to vessel structural failure
Long project cycles with delayed career advancement
motivation: Designing complex vessels that operate in extreme environments
Combining multiple engineering disciplines in one role
Contributing to maritime safety and environmental protection
Passion for maritime industry and vessels
burnout_factors: Travel requirements for construction oversight and sea trials
Small teams requiring broad technical coverage

community.summary: SNAME (Society of Naval Architects and Marine Engineers) is the primary US professional society. Strong ties to classification societies and maritime industry.

associations.name: SNAME (Society of Naval Architects and Marine Engineers)
associations.description: Primary US professional society, conferences, publications

associations.name: RINA (Royal Institution of Naval Architects)
associations.description: International professional body for naval architecture

associations.name: Marine Technology Society (MTS)
associations.description: Ocean engineering and marine technology community

conferences: International Conference on Ocean, Offshore and Arctic Engineering (OMAE)

market.summary: Niche market with 6% projected growth 2024-2034. ~600 annual openings. Median salary $106K. Driven by Navy shipbuilding programs, offshore wind, and commercial fleet modernization.
top_employers: US Navy shipyards (HII, General Dynamics NASSCO, Bath Iron Works)
market_trends: US Navy shipbuilding programs driving strong demand
Offshore wind industry creating new design opportunities
Decarbonization of shipping requiring new propulsion designs
Arctic shipping routes opening new design challenges
